identity.title: Let Features Decide Their Own Solvers: Hybrid Feature Caching for Diffusion Transformers

problem.claim: Diffusion Transformers face a sampling-time bottleneck because each timestep requires an expensive transformer forward pass.

gap.claim: Existing feature-caching methods often use one uniform strategy across feature dimensions, overlooking their heterogeneous dynamics.

contributions.claim: Introduces HyCa, a training-free hybrid caching framework that models hidden-feature evolution as dimension-wise mixtures of ODEs and selects caching strategies per dimension.
Reports near-lossless acceleration across diverse tasks and models without retraining.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish HyCa through dimension-wise caching derived from a mixture-of-ODEs view of hidden-feature evolution.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report speedups of 5.55× on FLUX, 5.56× on HunyuanVideo, and 6.24× on both Qwen-Image and Qwen-Image-Edit, without retraining.

narrative_sequence.summary: Diffusion Transformer sampling is costly because of repeated forward passes at every timestep.
Feature caching offers training-free acceleration, but existing approaches commonly treat all feature dimensions uniformly despite differing dynamics.
HyCa models feature evolution as dimension-wise ODE mixtures, applies hybrid caching strategies, and is reported to provide near-lossless multi-model acceleration.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links heterogeneous feature dynamics to a dimension-wise mixture-of-ODEs model and then to dimension-wise caching strategies.

lessons.interpretation: A method can become more targeted when its design explicitly reflects heterogeneity in the object being approximated.
lessons.application: When proposing an approximation method, partition components by their observed or modeled dynamics and assign specialized approximation rules rather than imposing one global policy.
lessons.exception: This move may be unsuitable when component-level dynamics are unavailable, too costly to estimate, or do not support stable specialization.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the baseline caching methods, evaluation protocol, or the quantitative meaning of “near-lossless.”
It does not report task-level quality metrics, latency measurement conditions, or whether all listed speedups use comparable hardware and settings.
